items.title: Audit and incrementally refactor repository hygiene, SOLID/SRP, and GEVP-to-C++ boundaries
items.description: Perform an evidence-first architectural stabilization milestone before the next feature. First audit tracked debris, generated artifacts, dead code, duplicated or contradictory documentation, and current runtime references. Then execute focused, behavior-preserving refactor stages only where verified by the repository: repository hygiene; documentation source-of-truth consolidation; removal of proven obsolete architecture; explicit read-only VehicleState boundary and separate command adapter; camera SRP; audio SRP; and the smallest justified move toward typed data-driven vehicle configuration. Do not blindly implement the external audit report; current repository, scenes, tests, AGENTS.md, and runtime behavior are authoritative.
items.rationale: The product owner selected architectural stabilization as the next milestone after the active HUD and vegetation work. Feature work and physics tuning will compound debt unless ownership, dead architecture, documentation authority, and the GEVP/GDScript-to-native presentation boundary are audited first.
items.technical_risk: High. This spans tracked assets, native C++, GDScript, Godot scenes, documentation, and build tooling. It must be staged with baseline behavior evidence, focused commits, scene-safety validation, and no handling retuning.
items.user_value: Creates a smaller, clearer, testable baseline that makes future vehicle, camera, audio, graphics, AI, and multi-agent changes safer.
acceptance_criteria: A repository audit report classifies tracked files and records evidence before deletion or untracking.
Every suspected obsolete system, including DirectionalVehicleSprite, is confirmed, partially confirmed, or rejected by references from code, scenes, resources, build files, tests, and documentation.
GEVP remains the physical simulation authority; native presentation consumers do not become a second physics engine.
Vehicle read state and vehicle mutation are separated only after current consumer requirements are verified.
Camera and audio responsibility splits are incremental and preserve observable behavior unless a separately documented bug is fixed.
No physics tuning is mixed into refactor commits; acceleration, braking, steering, grip, suspension, transmission, reset, camera, audio, HUD telemetry, and scene loading are regression-checked.
Every stage builds, runs relevant automated and Godot smoke tests, checks stale references, and updates current architecture documentation with verified results.
No generated artifact, source asset, third-party dependency, or local developer data is removed merely because it is large or ignored.
evidence: User-provided FORMULA-90 repository cleanup, SOLID/SRP and Clean Code refactor audit, 2026-08-10.
PROJECT_STATE.md: current architecture and technical-debt state.
docs/architecture.md and docs/architecture/: current architecture references.
native/src/core/game_bootstrap.cpp and game/scenes/runtime/world_hud_compositor.gd: current mixed native/GDScript runtime boundary.
README.md: current project stack and runtime claims.
items.source_context: User selected this as the next milestone after active UI HUD and vegetation increments, 2026-08-10.

items.title: Pair telemetry CSV with immutable _setup.json snapshots
items.description: Extend telemetry_manager.gd so every telemetry capture writes a paired <session>_setup.json snapshot generated from actual runtime values (provenance, chassis, tires, steering, brakes, differential, suspension, engine, transmission, aerodynamics, assists, surfaces) per PROJECT_STATE.md sections 13-19.
items.rationale: PROJECT_STATE.md declares setup pairing the REQUIRED gate before Phase C. Existing game/telemetry/*.csv captures have no setup provenance, so they cannot be attributed to a physical setup or compared safely.
items.technical_risk: Low. TelemetryManager is project-owned (game/addons/formula90s/scripts/telemetry_manager.gd); no vendor code touched. Schema is already proposed in PROJECT_STATE.md section 16.
items.user_value: Enables evidence-based physics decisions; prevents interpreting unprovenanced telemetry as authority.
acceptance_criteria: Each CSV capture produces a _setup.json with identical basename.
Setup JSON values are read from runtime vehicle node, not typed manually.
Changing a physical parameter during a run starts a new session/CSV.
Missing optional families remain explicit in JSON instead of invented.

items.title: Capture verified baseline telemetry with setup provenance
items.description: After PHY-001, record a reference telemetry session of the current validated Phase B Jordan setup (jordan_1995_phase_b.tscn on la_chutana_generated) to freeze a measurable baseline before any tuning.
items.rationale: No existing capture can be attributed to a known setup. A verified baseline is required to detect regressions across Phases C-G and to investigate the observed 2nd-gear top speed.
items.technical_risk: Low. Requires only PHY-001 and a controlled driving run.
items.user_value: Single source of truth for future physics comparisons.
acceptance_criteria: At least one paired CSV+_setup.json captured on la_chutana_generated with Phase B scene.
Session records vehicle scene, track scene, git commit and aid state.
Baseline CSV contains full-throttle straight and at least one braking/corner sequence.
evidence: Existing telemetry top speed 195.2 km/h and gears -1..2 only: game/telemetry/telemetry_20260809_191812_160.csv

items.title: Update physics_diagnostics defaults to Jordan Phase B configuration
items.description: Refresh tools/physics_diagnostics defaults (mass 505 kg, tire radii/widths, weights, wheelbase, tracks, powertrain) to mirror jordan_1995_phase_b.tscn instead of f1_2026_car.tscn (708 kg). Verify tscn_parser.py can read the Jordan scene.
items.rationale: All offline diagnostic scripts currently produce numbers for a 708 kg 2026 car; results are misleading for the 1995 Jordan and cannot be used as validation authority.
items.technical_risk: Low-medium. Scripts take overrides on the CLI; defaults must match the canonical Phase B scene exactly to keep offline/runtime agreement.
items.user_value: Restores trust in offline validation used by Phases D/E/F.
acceptance_criteria: run_all_diagnostics.py reports flags computed from Jordan Phase B values.
Documented comparison: old vs new default-derived top speed / spring frequencies.
No source of truth change: values match runtime scene.

items.title: Correct 1995 tire widths and wheel masses
items.description: Change front_tire_width 335->254 mm and rear_tire_width 420->325 mm (Goodyear slick era 1993-1997) and wheel masses 12/16 kg -> ~10/12 kg in jordan_1995.tscn Phase A values.
items.rationale: Width enters the friction load-sensitivity term friction = mu*F - F/(width*contact_patch*0.2) (wheel.gd:301). The current 335/420 mm belong to a later era; narrower 1995 tires reduce grip under load transfer, a core 1995 handling trait. Mass is physical authority from Phase A.
items.technical_risk: Medium. Reopens [VALIDATED] Phase A physical values; affects load transfer balance. Must be validated on jordan_handling_test.tscn before Phase C tuning starts, and Phase B values stay untouched.
items.user_value: Foundation for 1995 mechanical-grip character; affects all later phases.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime values confirmed as 254/325 mm and ~10/12 kg.
No Phase B parameter (friction, contact patch, brake bias, differential) changed.
Baseline telemetry re-captured after change (paired with setup JSON).
evidence: Reference: Wikipedia Formula_One_tyres (1993 rear width reduced 18in->15in, ~325 mm; front ~254 mm)

items.title: Correct 1995 track widths (wheel RayCast X positions)
items.description: Move front wheel RayCasts from X +/-0.739368 to +/-0.850 and rear from +/-0.718479 to +/-0.809 to match Jordan 195 front 1700 mm / rear 1618 mm track.
items.rationale: Track width drives the Ackermann correction (vehicle.gd:554-556) and roll-weight distribution; current tracks (1479/1437 mm) are narrower than the real 195 (1700/1618 mm).
items.technical_risk: Medium. Wheel RayCast positions are physical authority (PROJECT_STATE 5.1); visual wheel contract must remain symmetric; collision shapes and ackermann recompute automatically. Requires structural scene validation after edit.
items.user_value: Geometrically faithful 1995 platform for steering/suspension tuning.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime RayCast X positions match target track widths.
Visual wheel symmetry preserved (one visual per axle, 180-degree orientation).
Scene loads and drives without collision artifacts on jordan_handling_test.tscn.
evidence: Reference: Wikipedia Jordan_195 (front track 1700 mm, rear 1618 mm)

items.title: Correct 1995 tire radii (25in front / 26in rear maximums)
items.description: Change front/rear tire radius from 0.3473 m toward era maximums: front ~0.330 m (25 in), rear ~0.346 m (26 in).
items.rationale: Radius affects wheel speed conversion, tire-size correction and gearing. 1995 F1 max diameters were 25 in front / 26 in rear; current 0.3473 m equals 13.67 in radius (27.3 in diameter), slightly over era maximum.
items.technical_risk: Low-medium. Changing radius changes top speed per gear and contact geometry; keep both axles consistent with the max_tire_radius correction in vehicle.gd:492-494.
items.user_value: Small but correct era alignment; consistent gearing math in Phase E.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime radii match target values.
No Phase B/C/D parameter changed in the same commit.
evidence: Reference: Wikipedia Formula_One_tyres (diameter limits 25 in front / 26 in rear era)

items.title: Phase C: tune 1995 steering/countersteer progression
items.description: Replace baseline steering values with the PROJECT_STATE section 8.1 candidates (steering_speed ~3.7, countersteer_speed ~9.0, decay ~0.26, slip_assist ~0.11, countersteer_assist ~0.70, exponent ~1.70, max angle ~25 deg) and validate progressive keyboard response, unwind and recoverable-but-not-omniscient countersteer.
items.rationale: Steering is the next physics phase in the project roadmap (PROJECT_STATE section 8) and the first tuning step toward late-1990s formula feel (Monaco GP Racing Simulation 2 inspiration).
items.technical_risk: Medium. Must not touch tire/suspension/powertrain families simultaneously (phase discipline); telemetry pairing is required first; candidates are not validated values.
items.user_value: Readable, progressive steering - the first perceivable 1995 handling trait.
acceptance_criteria: Paired telemetry/setup records for every steering run.
Progressive keyboard response; predictable unwind; countersteer recoverable in time but a late correction still spins.
No regression in Phase B mechanical grip behavior.
Validated on multiple corners/speeds of la_chutana_generated.

items.title: Phase D: tune 1995 suspension behavior
items.description: Tune springs, damping, anti-roll and weight-transfer behavior toward stiff 1995 race setup (damping ratio 0.70-0.85, race bump/rebound split, balanced ARB) using telemetry for braking pitch, direction changes and curb response on la_chutana curbs (~22 mm rise).
items.rationale: Phase D is the suspension family phase; 1995 cars relied on mechanical grip with very stiff springs and strong damping. Current values are the known-good baseline (spring 0.15 m, resting 0.50, damping 0.75, bump 1.3, rebound 1.1, ARB 0.45/0.40).
items.technical_risk: Medium. Do not raise tire grip to conceal suspension problems; verify natural frequencies with analyze_suspension.py; bottom-out events (150 mm compression observed) must be diagnosed before curbs are blamed.
items.user_value: Mechanical, readable weight transfer - the core 1995 handling feel.
acceptance_criteria: No unexplained chassis bottom-out during reference curb test.
Front/rear natural frequencies documented and balanced.
No Phase B grip/brake values changed.
Paired telemetry for pitch/direction-change tests.

items.title: Phase E: implement 1995 Peugeot A10 V10 powertrain character
items.description: Replace the reference powertrain with a 1995-era V10 character: max_rpm ~15500, peak torque ~350 Nm with a peaky high-rpm torque curve, strong engine braking (motor_brake/motor_drag), preserving powertrain-philosophy.md (no hybrid/ERS).
items.rationale: The current engine (280 Nm @ 17000 rpm, curve (0,0.2)-(0.85,1.0)-(1.0,0.1)) is a placeholder, not 1995. The real Jordan 195 used the Peugeot A10 V10 (~700-760 hp @ 15500 rpm). Engine braking must be tactical per powertrain-philosophy.md.
items.technical_risk: High. Powertrain interacts with clutch model, auto-shift logic and traction; must not begin until mechanical handling (Phases C/D) is understood; validate offline with analyze_powertrain.py first.
items.user_value: The most iconic 1995 identity element: screaming high-revving V10.
acceptance_criteria: Torque curve and max_rpm verified offline before runtime tuning.
Engine braking is severe and tactically usable.
Top speed target (~300 km/h on la_chutana straight) measured with paired telemetry.
No hybrid/electrical system introduced.
evidence: Reference: Wikipedia Jordan_195 (Peugeot A10 3.0L V10 700-760 hp @ 15500 rpm)

items.title: Phase E: implement 7-speed 1995 transmission ratios
items.description: Extend gear_ratios from 6 to 7 elements with closer 1995-style ratios and adjust final drive so the V10 stays in its power band; the real Jordan 195 used a 7-speed semi-automatic gearbox.
items.rationale: Current 6-ratio set [2.85, 2.29, 1.89, 1.60, 1.38, 1.20] x 3.60 belongs to the reference placeholder. 7 speeds with a peaky engine require tighter spacing to exploit the narrow power band.
items.technical_risk: Medium. gear_ratios array size drives auto-shift thresholds in vehicle.gd:828-868; must be validated together with the V10 curve (PHY-008).
items.user_value: Authentic 1995 gearbox feel and shift cadence.
acceptance_criteria: Offline per-gear speed chart shows correct overlap/shift points.
Auto-shift selects all 7 gears on the straight (previous telemetry only reached gear 2).
Paired telemetry validates shift behavior.

items.title: Investigate automatic-transmission top-out in 2nd gear
items.description: Confirm or reject the hypothesis that the GEVP auto-shift logic never upshifts past gear 2 at ~195 km/h because upshifts require ideal (no-slip) wheel RPM above max_rpm. Use verified baseline telemetry (PHY-015) before touching vehicle.gd.
items.rationale: Observed in unprovenanced telemetry: max speed 195.2 km/h, max RPM 15896, gears -1..2 only. vehicle.gd:828-850 upshifts only when current_ideal_gear_rpm > max_rpm; if confirmed, the car never leaves low gears with the current curve.
items.technical_risk: Low. Research only; vehicle.gd is 'not pristine upstream' (PROJECT_STATE 4.3) so justified changes are possible, but require telemetry evidence first.
items.user_value: Prevents a powertrain tuning phase built on a transmission logic defect.
acceptance_criteria: Reproduction with paired telemetry on the verified baseline.
Documented root cause (or explicit rejection of the hypothesis).
Any change to vehicle.gd justified by measured behavior.

items.title: Validate Phase E powertrain offline (per-gear speeds, shift points)
items.description: Use analyze_powertrain.py with Jordan defaults (after PHY-002) to precompute torque/power curves, per-gear top speeds and ideal shift points for the new V10 and 7-speed gearbox before runtime tuning.
items.rationale: powertrain skill and ai_physics_manual mandate offline verification when engine tuning is involved; avoids runtime brute-force.
items.technical_risk: Low. Offline-only; requires PHY-002 defaults to be Jordan-accurate.
items.user_value: Fast deterministic validation of engine/gearbox pairing.
acceptance_criteria: Report documents power curve, per-gear top speed and shift RPM.
Report reviewed before runtime changes begin.

items.title: Phase F: implement 1995 speed-squared downforce layer
items.description: Create a project-owned (formula90s) speed-dependent downforce layer (V^2 scaling, front/rear split, high drag character) - no Formula90s aero layer exists today; GEVP only offers coefficient_of_drag/area.
items.rationale: 1995 cars had flat-bottom + wings: high drag, moderate downforce (~1.4-1.8x weight at top speed), rearward balance ~45-55%. Mechanical handling (Phases C/D) must already work so aero shapes only high-speed behavior.
items.technical_risk: High. New physics code in the project addon; must not mask mechanical grip problems; lift-off behavior must remain predictable; validate with analyze_aero_and_weight.py.
items.user_value: High-speed stability and era-authentic cornering at speed.
acceptance_criteria: Downforce scales with V^2 and is configurable in scene/inspector.
No downforce applied at rest/low speed (mechanical handling unchanged).
Balance front/rear adjustable without touching tire grip.

items.title: Validate Phase F aero balance offline
items.description: Precompute drag/downforce forces and weight transfer at reference speeds with analyze_aero_and_weight.py (after PHY-002 defaults fix) before runtime aero tuning.
items.rationale: aerodynamics skill requires offline precomputation of drag and weight transfer before altering GDScript.
items.user_value: Deterministic aero configuration instead of runtime guessing.
acceptance_criteria: Report covers drag and downforce at low/medium/high speed.
Front/rear balance documented at reference speeds.

items.title: Phase G: precise OFF semantics for driving aids
items.description: Separate natural vehicle physics, GEVP baseline stabilization and Formula90s optional aids (driving_aids.gd); define what 'OFF' means per aid (stability, steering, braking, grip, auto transmission) and make it measurable in telemetry.
items.rationale: PROJECT_STATE section 12: 'aid OFF' must have a precise behavioral meaning, not an undocumented fallback to hidden stabilization. 1995 cars had no ABS/TCS - wheel lock and spin must be possible.
items.technical_risk: Medium. Existing driving_aids.gd captures and restores baseline values; OFF semantics must be verified per aid without changing the natural physics already tuned in Phases C-F.
items.user_value: Authentic no-assists driving (era-correct risk) while keeping accessible assists.
acceptance_criteria: Each aid OFF state documented and verified in telemetry (no hidden stabilization).
Wheel lock under heavy braking and rear wheelspin on throttle possible with all aids OFF.
Aid ON/OFF toggles start new telemetry sessions.

items.title: Remodel the gameplay HUD with a dynamic La Chutana minimap
items.description: Replace the debug-oriented gameplay HUD with a late-1990s arcade racing presentation inspired by the supplied reference: a compact left-side circuit map, an oriented player marker updated from the vehicle transform, a visible start/finish marker, a bottom-right speed/gear gauge, and transient white top-right messages when a driving aid changes state. Preserve the world/HUD compositor boundary so UI remains outside world-only filtering.
items.rationale: The predecessor was a cyan diagnostic panel and its minimap was a hard-coded rectangle with arbitrary markers. La Chutana has a canonical centerline and start/finish data, so the player map can be accurate, simple, and real-time without coupling to visual track meshes.
items.technical_risk: Medium. The runtime compositor retargets HUD NodePaths after moving the scene outside WorldViewport. Preserve those paths, source aid-state changes from DrivingAidsController, and do not reintroduce HUD rendering inside WorldViewport.
items.user_value: A readable, authentic retro race HUD that makes speed, gear, player orientation, circuit layout, and the start point instantly legible.
acceptance_criteria: The gameplay HUD visually follows the supplied late-1990s arcade reference without copying logos or proprietary artwork.
The minimap draws the canonical La Chutana centerline, a distinct start/finish marker, and an oriented player marker that follows the vehicle in real time.
Speed and gear display actual vehicle runtime values; HUD remains crisp when world-only post-processing is enabled.
A white, background-free top-right message appears only when a driving aid is enabled or disabled, then fades without permanently occupying HUD space.
The legacy diagnostic/aids readout is not shown in normal gameplay and remains available only as an explicit debug/future feature.
A scene-load smoke test and a GPU visual capture validate the HUD at the active 16:9 presentation resolution.
items.source_context: User-requested HUD redesign based on supplied reference image, 2026-08-10

items.title: Add race-session data for lap, position, countdown, and rival markers
items.description: Implement a race-session authority that exposes real lap count, position, countdown/start lights, and opponent transforms to the HUD. The HUD composition should reserve/document these reference-inspired blocks, but it must not display invented values before this data exists.
items.rationale: The supplied HUD reference includes lap, position, a central countdown, and multiple map markers, but the current project has no race manager or opponent roster that can provide truthful values.
items.technical_risk: Medium-high. Requires a game-state/race progression owner rather than HUD-local counters; position must be derived from valid lap/progress data and not inferred from raw world coordinates alone.
items.user_value: Completes the race presentation with trustworthy progression and competition information once race gameplay exists.
acceptance_criteria: Lap, position, countdown, and rival markers are driven by a single authoritative race-session model.
No placeholder race values are visible in normal gameplay before the model is present.
Position and lap transitions are tested around the La Chutana start/finish line.
The minimap supports several player/opponent markers without obscuring the track outline.

items.title: HUD regression recovery: default bootstrap route HUD completeness
items.description: After the arcade HUD increment, the default GameBootstrap route (test_field.tscn) lacked a DrivingAids controller, so the visual capture could not toggle the aid notification and the full HUD contract was not exercised on the default route. Added the same DrivingAids node/script used by jordan_handling_test.tscn and re-validated the full mandatory suite.
items.rationale: Acceptance criterion for the HUD increment requires the default bootstrap route, not only jordan_handling_test.tscn, to support the aid notification and dynamic minimap tracking.
items.technical_risk: Low. Surgical scene edit adding one controller node already present in the reference handling scene; validated with scene-load and default-route smoke tests.
items.user_value: The normal game entry path shows the complete arcade HUD contract (minimap, gauge, transient aid message) from the first session.
acceptance_criteria: Default bootstrap route exercises minimap tracking, gauge readout and aid notification.
smoke_test_bootstrap_world_hud_compositor.gd passes on the default route.
visual_test_arcade_hud_capture.gd produces a 1280x720 capture with all HUD elements.
items.source_context: HUD regression recovery per instrucciones_deepseek.txt section 48, 2026-08-10. Surgical correction: smoke_test_jordan_skybox_runtime.gd camera-follow assertion needs two process frames for SourceSkyboxRig._process; single await was a one-frame race.
